To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a subset of patients with alcohol use disorder, identified by a machine learning model, is predicted to benefit from treatment with Gabapentin Enecarbil Extended-Release.

a randomized clinical trial of 338 patients with alcohol use disorder, who received either 600 mg twice daily gabapentin enacarbil extended release or placebo for 26 weeks, was reanalyzed using a machine learning approach to identify likely responders to treatment with gabapentin enecarbil extended release and to assess the causal superiority of gabapentin enencarbil extended release to placebo.

we identified a subset of patients who are likely to respond to treatment with gabapentin enacarbil extended release (GE‐XR) for alcohol use disorder (AUD) and that for this subset, GE‐XR is a superior treatment to placebo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of randomized clinical trials to identify likely responders and to determine whether the treatment is causally superior for likely responders.
the development of a statistical paradigm for analyzing randomized clinical trial data to identify subgroups that are likely responders to treatment.
the development of a statistical methodology to predict the response of patients to a treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GE‐XR was found to be causally superior to a placebo in reducing alcohol use in a subgroup of patients with a high probability of responding to GE‐XR.
the results of the present reanalysis suggest that the GE‐XR treatment may have a causal effect in a subset of patients with AUD.

the GE‐XR treatment is effective for reducing alcohol consumption in a subgroup of individuals with alcohol use disorder, and the GE‐XR is effective for improving sleep quality in all individuals with alcohol use disorders.

GE‐XR is effective in reducing alcohol use for a subset of people with AUD.
we have identified likely responders to GE-XR from the trial data.

the clinical trial of GE‐XR for treating alcohol use disorders was a success for a subset of the sample.
